text:
Linda (acme): Hey support - after we recreated a nodepool in eu-west our Dedicated > Capacity dashboard shows 0 nodes and 0 GPUs for that cluster. Customer is blocked, ticket #INC-4839. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.test/s/INC-4839.png

ben (support): sorry to hear that, escalating. When was the pool recreated? any label/annotation changes?

Linda (acme): pool was recreated 2026-03-04 ~14:22 UTC, we changed the k8s node annotation from `infra.group=old` -> `infra.group=new` as part of the migration. nodes look healthy in k8s though: `kubectl get nodes -l infra.group=new` shows all 6 nodes Ready.

ben (support): thanks. I'm pinging eng-infra and SRE to check inventory sync and analytics pipeline. @aisha @jordan

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-4839 (priority: P1) assigned to support-team

aisha (sre): looking now. Can you run `kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, labels:.metadata.labels}'` and paste one node's labels? suspect label rename lost mapping in the inventory pipeline.

Linda (acme): pasted one sample: `{name: node-07, labels: {"infra.group":"new","gpu.vendor":"nvidia.com","redwood.org/dedicated":"true"}}`

jordan (infra): querying inventory DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM node_inventory WHERE cluster_id='acme-eu-west'` -> returned 0. inventory service logs show: `WARN skipping node node-07: expected label infra.group=old not found`.

aisha (sre): aha. pipeline still expects the old annotation key/value. Looks like the reconciliation rule uses exact match for `infra.group` value. When pool was recreated we changed the value and the rego rule failed to classify nodes into dedicated pools.

ben (support): customer timeline: they need readout in dashboard within 1 hour or they'll escalate to legal. any quick workaround?

aisha (sre): quick workaround: run on the inventory coordinator host: `rctl inventory resync --cluster acme-eu-west --force` this forces a full re-eval of node labels against pool rules. It runs ~2-3m. I'll kick it.

jordan (infra): started job job-202603041523, logs: `resync started for acme-eu-west`, iterating 6 nodes. Patch applied: rule matcher now tolerates alias values.

ops-bot: Job job-202603041523 completed in 2m 14s

ben (support): Linda, can you refresh the Dedicated Capacity page?

Linda (acme): refreshed — nodes and GPUs returned! panel shows 6 nodes, 48 GPUs. thank you :relieved:

aisha (sre): root cause: reconciliation rules were keyed to the previous pool label value and the pool-recreate + label rename left the rulestore unchanged. Plan: ship a hotfix to make rule matching resilient to label renames, and add a metric + alert when inventory_count drops to zero after node lifecycle events.

jordan (infra): filed follow-up issue INFRA-1287 to update rulestore migration and add test coverage. Target release: 1.9.2.

ben (support): closing INC-4839 with workaround documented. Will follow up with customer postmortem and link to INFRA-1287.

Linda (acme): thanks all — appreciate the fast help.

aisha (sre): note for release notes: `Fixed inventory reconciliation for nodepool label renames; added resync endpoint for on-demand repair (rctl inventory resync)`.
